message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"2.37","text":"Some of our companions associate with Simon under false pretenses, as though they had been persuaded by his most godless error, so that, by learning his plans, they may disclose them to us, enabling us to adapt ourselves appropriately to a formidable man. And now I have learned from them the question about which he intends to deliver his arguments. When I learned this, I thanked God and counted you blessed because of the debate’s postponement; for, having been equipped by me before the debate, you will be able to hear without stumbling the arguments that he is going to present for the testing of those who do not know.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προσποιητῶς σύνεισιν","chosen":"associate ... under false pretenses","rationale":"The adverb indicates that their apparent association or agreement with Simon is feigned."},{"source_quote":"τῇ ἀθεωτάτῃ αὐτοῦ πλάνῃ","chosen":"his most godless error","rationale":"The rendering retains the superlative force of ἀθεωτάτῃ and the sense of πλάνη as religious error or deception."},{"source_quote":"δεινῷ ἀνδρὶ οἰκείως συναρμόσασθαι","chosen":"adapt ourselves appropriately to a formidable man","rationale":"συναρμόζομαι conveys fitting or adapting oneself, while δεινός may describe someone formidable, dangerous, or highly capable."},{"source_quote":"ἧς μέλλει ζητήσεως ποιεῖσθαι τοὺς λόγους","chosen":"the question about which he intends to deliver his arguments","rationale":"ζητήσεως identifies the disputed question or debate topic, while ποιεῖσθαι τοὺς λόγους refers to presenting arguments about it."},{"source_quote":"τῶν γὰρ μελλόντων λόγων ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ πρὸς διάκρισιν τῶν ἀγνοούντων λέγεσθαι ... ἄπτωτος ἀκροατὴς γενέσθαι δυνήσει","chosen":"you will be able to hear without stumbling the arguments that he is going to present for the testing of those who do not know","rationale":"The fronted genitive τῶν ... λόγων is taken with ἀκροατής as the content heard. διάκρισις can denote differentiation or judgment and is rendered “testing” because the clause presents Simon’s arguments as a means of exposing uninstructed hearers to a trial. Unlike the explicit πειρασμός, “test” or “trial,” in 2.39, however, διάκρισις may emphasize the resulting division, doubt, or perplexity. The alternative “to unsettle those who do not know” is supported by Simon’s attempt to alienate hearers in 2.39 and by διακριθῆναι, rendered “to waver,” in 2.40."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τῶν γὰρ μελλόντων λόγων ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ πρὸς διάκρισιν τῶν ἀγνοούντων λέγεσθαι σὺ πρὸ τῆς ζητήσεως ἐφοδιασθεὶς ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ ἄπτωτος ἀκροατὴς γενέσθαι δυνήσει.","issue":"The fronted genitive τῶν ... λόγων is most naturally attached to ἀκροατής, yielding the arguments Clement will hear without stumbling. Attachment to ἐφοδιασθείς, “equipped with the arguments,” is grammatically conceivable but less direct and is not adopted. In addition, πρὸς διάκρισιν τῶν ἀγνοούντων may mean “for the testing of those who do not know,” as translated, or “to unsettle those who do not know,” with διάκρισις emphasizing doubt or perplexity. The latter is contextually supported by 2.39 and by διακριθῆναι in 2.40. These are attachment and lexical ambiguities, not evidence of source corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.38","text":"For the writings took on many false statements against God for this reason: when the prophet Moses, by God’s counsel, had handed down the law together with its interpretations to some chosen persons, seventy in number, so that they too might equip those among the people who wished it, not long afterward, once the law had been put into writing, it took on some false statements against the sole God, who created heaven and earth and everything in them, because the evil one dared to bring this about for a certain just reason. And this happened with reason and judgment, so that it might be shown who dare eagerly to listen to the things written against God, and who, out of affection for him, not only disbelieve the things said against him but refuse to endure hearing them at all, even if they should happen to be true, judging it much safer to take a risk for reverent faith than to live with a troubled conscience over blasphemous words.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"αἱ γραφαὶ","chosen":"the writings","rationale":"The phrase denotes the authoritative written corpus under discussion without importing the boundaries or capitalization of a later canon."},{"source_quote":"γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ","chosen":"by God’s counsel","rationale":"γνώμη may mean judgment, purpose, decision, or counsel; “counsel” presents Moses’ transmission as occurring by divine determination."},{"source_quote":"ἐκλεκτοῖς τισὶν ἑβδομήκοντα","chosen":"some chosen persons, seventy in number","rationale":"This preserves both the indefinite force of τισίν and the stated number without making “some seventy” sound approximate."},{"source_quote":"δικαίῳ τινὶ λόγῳ","chosen":"for a certain just reason","rationale":"The phrase grammatically accompanies the evil one’s action. The difficult claim that his action occurred for a just reason is retained rather than reassigned to another agent."},{"source_quote":"τὰ κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ γραφέντα φιληκόως ἔχειν","chosen":"eagerly to listen to the things written against God","rationale":"φιληκόως expresses fondness for hearing or eagerness to listen, contrasting with the following group’s refusal even to hear such statements."},{"source_quote":"κἂν ἀληθῆ τυγχάνῃ","chosen":"even if they should happen to be true","rationale":"The antecedent is the things said against God. Greek permits the singular verb with the neuter plural predicate, and the author’s striking concession is retained."},{"source_quote":"περὶ εὐφήμου πίστεως κινδυνεύειν","chosen":"to take a risk for reverent faith","rationale":"εὔφημος concerns favorable or reverent speech, in contrast with the blasphemous words that follow. An alternative is “to take a risk for faith that speaks well of God.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"κἂν ἀληθῆ τυγχάνῃ; πολλῷ κρίναντες ἀσφαλέστερον· περὶ εὐφήμου πίστεως κινδυνεύειν ἢ ἐπὶ βλασφήμοις λόγοις δυσσυνειδήτως βιοῦν.","issue":"The supplied punctuation places a question mark after τυγχάνῃ and a middle dot after ἀσφαλέστερον, although κρίναντες and the following comparative infinitives form a coherent continuation of the preceding description. The translation treats the punctuation as editorial and follows the grammatical connection without altering the supplied Greek wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.39","text":"Simon, then, as I learn, intends to come into the midst and recite the very passages against God that were added to the writings for the sake of testing, so that he may be able to detach from affection for God as many wretched people as he can. For we do not wish to say publicly that these passages have been added to the books, since by alarming unlearned crowds we would be doing the will of the wicked Simon himself. Because they do not yet possess the ability to discern, they will either flee from us as impious or, supposing that falsity is not confined to the blasphemous passages, withdraw from the teaching. We are therefore compelled, while assenting to the false passages and asking him counterquestions about them, to bring him into perplexity, but privately, after a test of faith, to provide fair-minded people with the explanation of the passages spoken against God. That explanation has one brief path. It is this:","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πειρασμοῦ χάριν προσκειμένας","chosen":"added ... for the sake of testing","rationale":"πρόσκειμαι indicates that the passages were attached or added, while πειρασμός denotes a trial or test in this context."},{"source_quote":"ἐλθὼν εἰς μέσον λέγειν","chosen":"come into the midst and recite","rationale":"The rendering preserves the image of Simon entering the midst of the assembly and speaking the passages publicly."},{"source_quote":"πτύραντες ἀμαθεῖς ὄχλους","chosen":"by alarming unlearned crowds","rationale":"πτύρω means to frighten or alarm, and ἀμαθής describes people lacking instruction or learning."},{"source_quote":"ἢ ὡς οὐ μόνον τῶν βλασφήμων περικοπῶν ψευδῶν οὐσῶν ἀποστήσονται τοῦ λόγου","chosen":"or, supposing that falsity is not confined to the blasphemous passages, withdraw from the teaching","rationale":"The unexpressed counterpart to οὐ μόνον is understood as an extension of perceived falsity beyond the blasphemous passages to the larger teaching. A more formally literal rendering is “or, supposing that not only the blasphemous passages are false, they will withdraw from the teaching.”"},{"source_quote":"συγκατατιθέμενοι ταῖς ψευδέσι περικοπαῖς","chosen":"while assenting to the false passages","rationale":"The speakers accept the passages as the basis of the public argument; the wording does not require that they affirm the passages as true."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ εὐγνωμονοῦσιν τῶν κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ῥηθεισῶν περικοπῶν μετὰ πεῖραν πίστεως ἰδίᾳ παρέχειν τὴν ἐπίλυσιν","chosen":"privately, after a test of faith, to provide fair-minded people with the explanation of the passages spoken against God","rationale":"The genitive τῶν ... περικοπῶν is attached to τὴν ἐπίλυσιν, specifying what is explained. Alternatively, it may attach to εὐγνωμονοῦσιν: “to those who judge sensibly concerning the passages spoken against God.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἢ ὡς οὐ μόνον τῶν βλασφήμων περικοπῶν ψευδῶν οὐσῶν ἀποστήσονται τοῦ λόγου","issue":"The coordination is elliptical because οὐ μόνον has no expressed corresponding member. The translation understands an implied extension of falsity beyond the blasphemous passages to the larger teaching. The supplied wording nevertheless admits a defensible contextual translation and need not be emended.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ εὐγνωμονοῦσιν τῶν κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ῥηθεισῶν περικοπῶν μετὰ πεῖραν πίστεως ἰδίᾳ παρέχειν τὴν ἐπίλυσιν","issue":"The genitive τῶν ... περικοπῶν may specify τὴν ἐπίλυσιν, “the explanation of the passages,” as adopted in the translation, or it may depend on εὐγνωμονοῦσιν, describing people who judge sensibly concerning those passages. This is an ordinary attachment ambiguity rather than source corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.40","text":"Everything said or written against God is false. That we say this truly, not merely for reverence’s sake but also for truth’s, I will fully demonstrate when the discussion has advanced a little. Therefore you, my dearest Clement, ought not to be grieved that Simon has postponed the debate for a single day—the present one. For since today, before the debate, you are being equipped in advance concerning the passages added to the writings, you ought not to waver during the debate concerning the sole and good God, who also made the world. Instead, during the debate you will even marvel at how the impious pass over the many things said in the writings on God’s behalf, yet look around for the things said against him and joyfully bring them forward. Thus the hearers, because of ignorance, believe the things said against God and become excluded from his kingdom. Therefore, having learned the mystery of the writings on the occasion of the postponement and having gained the benefit of not sinning against God, you will show favor beyond compare.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εὐφημίας ἕνεκεν","chosen":"for reverence’s sake","rationale":"εὐφημία here concerns speaking favorably or reverently of God, in contrast with the surrounding blasphemous statements."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ βραχὺ προϊόντος τοῦ λόγου πληροφορήσω","chosen":"I will fully demonstrate when the discussion has advanced a little","rationale":"πληροφορέω conveys providing full assurance or establishing something fully, while λόγος denotes the developing discussion or argument."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τοῦ μόνου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ θεοῦ","chosen":"concerning the sole and good God","rationale":"The rendering preserves μόνος and ἀγαθός as coordinated descriptions. An alternative is “concerning the only God, who is good.”"},{"source_quote":"διακριθῆναι","chosen":"to waver","rationale":"In this context διακρίνω denotes divided judgment, doubt, or uncertainty rather than analytical discernment."},{"source_quote":"τὰ πλήθη τῶν ὑπὲρ θεοῦ εἰρημένων","chosen":"the many things said ... on God’s behalf","rationale":"The rendering preserves the contrast between the abundance of favorable statements and the selectively cited statements against God."},{"source_quote":"τὰ κατ’ αὐτοῦ εἰρημένα περιβλεπόμενοι χαίροντες φέρουσιν","chosen":"look around for the things said against him and joyfully bring them forward","rationale":"περιβλέπομαι retains the image of looking around or searching, χαίροντες supplies their delight, and φέρουσιν describes bringing the selected statements forward."},{"source_quote":"προφάσει ὑπερθέσεως","chosen":"on the occasion of the postponement","rationale":"πρόφασις may mean occasion, stated reason, or pretext. “On the occasion” presents the delay as the opportunity for instruction without requiring deceptive intent."},{"source_quote":"ἀπαραβλήτως χαρίσῃ","chosen":"you will show favor beyond compare","rationale":"The translation follows the ordinary benefactive force of χαρίζομαι and leaves the recipient unexpressed, as in the supplied Greek. It does not import the meaning “rejoice” from the conjectural χαρήσῃ."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀπαραβλήτως χαρίσῃ","issue":"The supplied χαρίσῃ can be read as a future middle form of χαρίζω, but its benefactive sense is contextually difficult because no recipient or object is expressed. The main translation therefore remains provisional and preserves the printed verb’s sense without supplying a recipient. The conjecture χαρήσῃ would straightforwardly mean “you will rejoice beyond compare,” but it is not the supplied reading and is not used to justify the translation.","proposed_reading":"χαρήσῃ","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
